title: Terraform module: GPU instance pool orchestration with ASG/Karpenter failover and health hooks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that manages GPU instance pools for Private (VPC) deployments with transparent orchestration between ASG and Karpenter. The module must provide safe upgrade paths, graceful drain/eviction hooks tied to the Redwood serving runtime, spot/preemptible GPU handling, and automated failover policies so customer workloads meet latency and availability SLOs during scale events and node upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes configurable provider switch: asg_mode | karpenter_mode; both paths produce identical node labels and taints used by Redwood runtime
Can perform in-place minor driver/kernel upgrades with <5% qps impact on benchmark workload (measured on staging)
Graceful drain hook implemented: runtime drain RPC triggered and KV cache warmed for replacement nodes before traffic routed
Preemptible/spot handling: waves of spot terminations trigger automatic replacement and capacity fallback to reserved instances without request errors
Terraform plan/apply for module can run in private VPC without modifying cluster-level RBAC beyond documented role bindings
Module has comprehensive unit tests (terratest) and example configs for both ASG and Karpenter usage
tasks: Draft module API and variables (instance types, gpu_profile, drain_timeout, eviction_strategy, warmup_hook)
Implement ASG path: launch templates, healthcheck hooks, lifecycle hooks to call runtime drain endpoint
Implement Karpenter path: provisioner spec, taints/labels, lifecycle hook emulation via preStop and admission webhooks
Add Spot/Preemptible strategy: fallback pools, capacity-provision policies, cost bucket metrics
Write terratest suite against a local KIND/eksctl staging cluster and CI pipeline
Create example overlay for private-deploys with gated IAM roles and KMS references
Document upgrade procedure and rollback playbook in Confluence
File and validate security review (KMS/HSM interactions and audit logging)
notes: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — aligned on single module supporting both ASG and Karpenter via provider switch. Trade-off: duplicating lifecycle bits vs exposing unified abstraction. Decided to keep separate implementations behind a common variable to reduce complexity in each path.
2026-03-11: Spike shows kernel-module updates cause longer drain times on older CUDA images. Plan: add fast-rollback path that re-attaches previous AMI and marks new nodes cordoned.
2026-03-12: Design review feedback (PM/Runtime): require explicit warmup hook that pre-populates KV cache for LLM inference. Added warmup_hook variable and API for runtime to register endpoint.
2026-03-13: Security noted need to avoid storing private keys in state — switching to remote state with CMK-wrapped S3 and adding a pre-apply checklist for IAM reviewers.

2026-03-14: Implementation: ASG lifecycle hook prototype done. Karpenter emulation approach (preStop webhook + node annotation) under review. Open question: how to signal streaming requests in-flight — runtime team suggests small grace window + sticky-router update.
Follow-ups: measure end-to-end failover latency under spike; add automated canary draining job; create dashboard for per-node warmup success rate.
